subject.title: feat(system-agent): agentic cached caretaker greeting with quick actions

question: Should the core system-agent rescue/setup flow adopt a model-phrased cached caretaker greeting and quick-action chips as its default welcome behavior?
rationale: This is a new user-facing identity and inference behavior in the protected system-agent surface; tests can validate mechanics but cannot establish whether this is the intended long-term product boundary for the core setup path.

options.title: Sponsor and require runtime proof
options.body: Keep the feature in core, after adding inspectable redacted proof for rendering, cache reuse, and delivery-gated retry behavior.

options.title: Keep the deterministic welcome
options.body: Decline the model-generated greeting direction and retain a concise deterministic welcome with only existing setup guidance.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Accept deterministic quick actions and status facts while deferring model phrasing until the system-agent product direction is settled.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and require runtime proof
recommendation.body: Keep the feature in core, after adding inspectable redacted proof for rendering, cache reuse, and delivery-gated retry behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The related overhaul proposal and merged session-ownership work make this the strongest available routing signal for the intended system-agent direction.
